title: Pattern Root Edits require both an alignment finding and a quorate token holder majority
content:
The approval condition in A.6.1.1.6.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.4 is conjunctive: the Snapshot poll "is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have 50% of votes in favor to be approved."

Quorum and majority do different jobs. The participation floor guards against a tiny, motivated minority carrying a change through apathy; the majority requirement decides direction among those who show up. Together with the Facilitator's prior alignment finding, a Root Edit therefore needs **two independent kinds of legitimacy** — procedural/normative from the reviewer, and economic from the holders.

A.6.1.1.6.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.5 closes the loop asymmetrically: if approved, "the Operational Facilitator submits the edit to Powerhouse to formally update the Agent Artifact," but *regardless of outcome*, the Facilitator "updates the Powerhouse System to include the result of the vote, including any pertinent documents." Failed proposals are recorded, not discarded — the record of what was rejected is treated as part of the Artifact's history.

The short three-day window is the notable cost. Combined with a 10% quorum, it demands rapid mobilization of a meaningful share of supply, which in practice advantages coordinated or delegated holders over dispersed ones.
description: A three-day Snapshot poll needs at least 10% of circulating supply participating and 50% in favor; the Facilitator then submits the approved edit and must publish the outcome either way.
